notes.ntunza: Often used for selling as a business.

guidebook.intro: Small businesses keep Uganda running: market stalls, kiosks, tailors and boda bodas. This unit adds verbs for making someone else do something.

tips.title: Making someone do: -is- / -es-
body: Add **-is-** or **-es-** before the last vowel to mean “make someone do” or “help someone do”: **-soma** (read) becomes **-somesa** (teach), **-lya** (eat) becomes **-lisa** (feed), **-nywa** (drink) becomes **-nywesa** (give a drink).
You already know one: **omusomesa** (teacher) is literally “one who makes people read”.

culture.title: Savings groups
body: Many people save in groups: members pay in every week and take turns receiving the pot. These groups also lend to members, so a debt (**ebanja**) is owed to friends, not a bank.
